description: Composite four-panel figure (declared type mixed: crystal-structure models plus electron micrographs). (a) is a ball-and-stick cube model labelled "(Fe, Mn)Al-type B2 phase": white solid edges with dashed hidden edges, black spheres labelled Fe/Mn, red spheres labelled C along the cell edges, and one yellow sphere near the cube centre whose label is not printed. (b) is the equivalent cube labelled "NiAl-type B2 phase", built from orange spheres labelled Ni plus a single green sphere labelled Al at the cube centre. (c) is an electron (SEM-type) micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar showing three annotated B2 morphologies in a lighter matrix: "Blocky" inside a white dashed rectangle marked (2) at top left, "Banded" in the middle marked (1), and "Ultrafine" inside a white dashed rectangle marked (3) near the bottom. (d) is a TEM bright-field image with a printed 500 μm scale bar (likely 500 nm) showing a rounded B2 particle in a γ matrix criss-crossed by dislocations, plus an inset (also printed 500 μm) with a smaller B2 particle in γ. Together the panels define the two B2 ordering types and show the three B2 precipitate morphologies and the dislocation structure at B2/γ interfaces that the citing text links to work hardening. No axes or numeric data are plotted; only scale bars carry numbers.
measured_quantities: scale bar length of micrograph (c): 10 µm
scale bar length printed on TEM image (d) and its inset: 500 μm (as printed; probably 500 nm)
B2 precipitate morphology / feature size class (banded, blocky, ultrafine)

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a cube model printed with the label '(Fe, Mn)Al-type B2 phase', with black spheres annotated Fe/Mn, red spheres annotated C, and one yellow sphere near the cube centre carrying no printed label.
Panel (b) is the same cube geometry printed with the label 'NiAl-type B2 phase', with orange spheres annotated Ni and one green sphere annotated Al at the cube centre.
Panel (c) is an electron micrograph with a 10 µm scale bar in which the words 'Blocky' (dashed box 2), 'Banded' (1) and 'Ultrafine' (dashed box 3) are printed over a two-phase light/dark structure.
Panel (d) shows a bright-field TEM image with a rounded B2 particle embedded in a γ matrix containing many dislocation lines, plus an inset showing a smaller B2 particle in γ.

Both scale bars in panel (d) — main image and inset — are printed as '500 μm', a value that is physically implausible for a TEM micrograph and presumably intended as 500 nm; the printed text is not consistent with the microscopy scale.
No axes, curves, data labels or numeric values are present in any panel; the only printed numerals are the scale-bar lengths (10 µm in (c), 500 μm in (d)) and the region tags (1), (2), (3) in (c).
The caption states that (a, b) show the lattice of B2 phase and NiAl ordered phases in Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steel [69], and that (c, d) show B2 phase precipitates in aged Fe-Mn-Al-C steel [71].

The citing text reports that after cold rolling and annealing the Fe-16Mn-9.6Al-0.86C-4.9Ni steel contains three B2 morphologies (banded, blocky and ultrafine), which corresponds to the three labels printed in panel (c).

The citing text attributes the banded B2 to transformation from δ-ferrite (white rectangle area), the blocky B2 along recrystallized austenite grain boundaries to transformation from α-ferrite (yellow rectangle area), and the ultrafine B2 to nucleation on shear bands of recrystallized austenite grains (red rectangle area); only white dashed rectangles are visible in panel (c), so the yellow and red rectangle markings could not be confirmed in the pixels.

The citing text states that B2 phase is an ordered body-centred cubic structure of CsCl type, as shown in Fig. 6a and b, and that (Fe, Mn)Al or NiAl type ordered intermetallic compounds form during quenching-aging/cold rolling-annealing of Fe-Mn-Al-C low density steels.

The citing text states that, unlike κ-carbide, B2 phase is not sheared by slip dislocations, leading to dislocation pile-up at the phase boundary and enhanced work hardening (Fig. 6d), which is the behaviour illustrated by the dislocation structure around the B2 particle in panel (d).

The first citing sentence assigns the L'12 ordered structure of κ-carbide to 'Fig. 6 [63]', whereas this figure's caption describes only B2/NiAl lattices and B2 precipitates; the panels contain no κ-carbide L'12 lattice model, so the citation and the figure caption disagree.

subfigures.description: Ball-and-stick cube model of the (Fe, Mn)Al-type B2 phase: black spheres labelled Fe/Mn at corner and cell positions, red spheres labelled C, and one yellow sphere near the centre with no printed label. Solid white lines are visible edges, dashed lines hidden edges.
Ball-and-stick cube model of the NiAl-type B2 phase: orange spheres labelled Ni and a single green sphere labelled Al at the cube centre, drawn in the same cube geometry as (a).

Electron micrograph (SEM-type contrast) with a 10 µm scale bar; three B2 morphologies annotated in the light/dark two-phase structure: 'Blocky' in a white dashed rectangle (2) top-left, 'Banded' centre (1), 'Ultrafine' in a white dashed rectangle (3) bottom.

TEM bright-field image of a rounded B2 particle in a γ matrix with dense dislocation lines; magnified inset at bottom-left shows a second, smaller B2 particle in γ. Both scale bars are printed as 500 μm, which is implausible for a TEM micrograph.

unreadable_items: panel (a): the label of the yellow sphere near the cube centre is not printed / not legible (the red spheres are labelled C)
panel (d): scale bars are printed '500 μm' in both the main image and the inset; the unit/order of magnitude for a TEM image cannot be confirmed (probably nm)
panel (c): the yellow and red rectangle areas described in the citing text are not identifiable — only the white dashed rectangles (2) and (3) and the numbered tag (1) are visible
panel (c): the specific imaging mode (SE vs BSE) and any phase identification of the dark/light constituents are not stated on the image
